### How Period Closing Works

#### 1. Select the Period

The user selects a **From Date** and **To Date**, defining the accounting period being closed.

#### 2. Review and Finalise All Transactions

Before closing the period, the organisation must manually ensure the following tasks are completed:

**Manual Tax Reconciliation (Required)**

- Reconcile VAT/GST collected & paid
- Verify tax ledgers (input tax, output tax, adjustments)
- Confirm that taxable transactions match the tax summary
- Ensure no missing or incorrect tax entries exist
- Reconcile with external systems or portals if required (e.g., FTA Portal – UAE)

*This manual tax reconciliation must be completed before the Period Closing Voucher is submitted.*

**General Reconciliation Checks**

- Bank reconciliation
- Vendor & customer reconciliation
- Ledger matching
- Final review of journals and adjustments

#### 3. System Settlement of Profit & Loss

Once submitted, DIGITZ ERP:

- Identifies all Profit & Loss accounts
- Calculates net profit or loss for the selected period
- Automatically transfers the value to the chosen Balance Sheet account (e.g., Retained Earnings)

#### 4. Locking the Period

After submission:

- No new transactions can be posted in the closed period
- No edits or cancellations are allowed
- Ensures historical accuracy and audit compliance

### Why Tax Reconciliation Must Be Manual

DIGITZ ERP intentionally **does not automate tax reconciliation** during period closing because:

- Tax computations may require cross-checking with government portals
- Some adjustments may be handled outside the ERP
- Tax filing rules vary between countries and reporting periods
- Manual review ensures accuracy and prevents incorrect tax reporting

This makes the process compliant, safe, and audit-ready.

### Typical Use Cases

- Quarterly closing for management performance review
- Half-year and annual closing for audit and financial reporting
- Preparing books before statutory tax filing
- Locking historical data to maintain consistency

### Future Enhancements *(Planned)*

- **Taxation Closing** *(Future Enhancement)* — Automated tax settlement and tax-period computations.
- **Voucher Edit Locking** *(Future Enhancement)* — Advanced locking rules for vouchers within closed periods.
- **Extended Compliance Tools** *(Future Enhancement)* — Automated reconciliation aids for tax and financial audits.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Stock Module Overview
entries.content:
The **Stock Module** in **DIGITZ ERP** maintains the item masters, warehouses, units, and price lists used across the system, and records every movement of goods through a single **Stock Ledger**.

Stock is valued on a **moving average** basis. Each ledger row stores the quantity in and out, the incoming or outgoing rate, and the resulting **Balance Qty**, **Balance Value**, and **Valuation Rate** for that item in that warehouse — so the stock position and its value are always available at any point in time.

The ledger is written by both the stock documents and the trading documents: **Purchase Receipt**, **Purchase Invoice**, **Purchase Return**, **Delivery Note**, **Sales Invoice**, **Sales Return**, **Stock Transfer**, **Stock Entry**, **Material Issue**, and **Stock Reconciliation**. Physical movement and financial posting therefore stay aligned without separate data entry.

Because documents can be recorded with a back date, the module also maintains a **reposting mechanism**. When an entry is posted earlier than existing movements, the affected ledger rows are recalculated forward in time and the item's stock balance and cost of goods sold are corrected.

Only items with **Maintain Stock** enabled generate stock ledger entries. Service, labour, and fixed asset items are excluded from stock movement while still participating in buying and selling documents.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Item
entries.content:
The **Item** master in **DIGITZ ERP** holds a single definition of everything the system needs in order to buy, sell, store, and value a product or a service.

### Purpose

To maintain one authoritative record per item — its identity, unit of measure, grouping, tax treatment, expense account, and prices — which every transaction across the system refers to.

### How It Works

Items are identified by **Item Code**. When **Auto Generate Item Code** is enabled on the Company, the code is generated from the **Short Code** of the selected **Item Group** (producing codes such as `ABC-000001`); if the item group has no short code, the series `IT-######` is used instead.

Each item carries a **Base Unit**, which is the unit the stock ledger is maintained in. Further units can be listed in the **Units** table with a conversion factor against the base unit — the base unit itself is always added automatically with a conversion factor of 1.

The **Item Type** determines how the item behaves: `Product`, `Non Stock`, `Service`, `Labour`, `Material`, `Fixed Asset`, `BOQ Product`, or `BOM Product`. **Maintain Stock** controls whether the item produces stock ledger entries; for a **Fixed Asset** item it is switched off automatically, since stock is not maintained for assets.

**Standard Selling Price** and **Standard Buying Price** entered on the item are written through to the `Standard Selling` and `Standard Buying` price lists as **Item Price** records every time the item is saved — created when absent, and updated when the rate has changed.

### Key Fields

- **Item Code** - Unique identifier for the item, generated automatically when auto-generation is enabled on the Company.
- **Item Name** - Descriptive name of the item.
- **Base Unit** - The unit in which stock is maintained for the item.
- **Item Group** - Classification of the item; also supplies the default expense account and the short code used for automatic coding.
- **Brand** - Optional brand the item belongs to.
- **Tax** - Tax applicable to the item, along with **Tax Not Applicable** for exempt items.
- **Item Type** - Determines whether the item is a product, service, labour, material, fixed asset, or BOQ/BOM product.
- **Maintain Stock** - Determines whether the item generates stock ledger entries.
- **Default Expense Account** - The account charged when the item is expensed.
- **Units** - Table of alternate units with their conversion factors against the base unit.
- **Customer Prices / Supplier Prices** - Party-specific rates for the item.
- **Stock Balance (Base Unit)**, **Stock Value**, **Valuation Rate** - Read-only figures maintained by the stock posting and reposting routines.

### Validations

- The **Base Unit** cannot be changed once stock ledger entries exist for the item in a different unit.
- A **Service** item cannot use a **Cost of Goods Sold** account as its Default Expense Account.
- The Company must have a **Default Product Expense Account** configured before an item can be saved.
- When no description is entered, the item name is used as the description.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Item Group
entries.content:
The **Item Group** in **DIGITZ ERP** classifies items and supplies defaults that are applied when items are created.

### Purpose

To organise the item master into meaningful categories and to hold the accounting and coding defaults shared by all items in that category.

### How It Works

Each item is linked to an item group. The group can carry a **Default Expense Account**, which is used as the expense head for items in the group, and a **Short Code**, which drives automatic item code generation when the Company has **Auto Generate Item Code** enabled.

Item groups are also used as a reference type for budgeting, so a budget can be set against a group rather than an individual item, and as a grouping dimension in the stock and purchase analysis reports.

### Key Fields

- **Item Group Name** - Name of the group.
- **Short Code** - Prefix used when generating item codes automatically.
- **Default Expense Account** - Expense account applied to items in this group.
- **Description** - Optional descriptive text.
- **Image** - Optional image for the group.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Unit and Unit Conversion
entries.content:
**Units** in **DIGITZ ERP** allow an item to be transacted in a unit different from the one it is stocked in, while the stock ledger is always maintained in a single consistent unit.

### Purpose

To let users buy, sell, and move goods in whichever unit is practical for the transaction, without losing the ability to value and report stock in one common unit.

### How It Works

Every item has a **Base Unit**, and the stock ledger is always kept in that unit. Alternate units are listed in the item's **Units** table together with a **Conversion Factor** expressing how many base units one alternate unit represents. The base unit is always present with a conversion factor of 1.

When a unit other than the base unit is selected on a transaction line, the system converts the entered quantity and rate and stores both forms on the row — **Qty** and **Rate** as entered, and **Qty In Base Unit** and **Rate In Base Unit** as posted. The **Unit Conversion Details** field records the conversion that was applied, so the line remains auditable.

Because the ledger is written in base units, all stock reports, valuation, and balances remain directly comparable regardless of the unit used at entry.

### Key Fields

- **Unit** - The unit selected on the transaction line.
- **Conversion Factor** - Number of base units represented by one of the selected units.
- **Qty In Base Unit** - Quantity converted into the item's base unit, used for all stock postings.
- **Rate In Base Unit** - Rate converted into the item's base unit.
- **Unit Conversion Details** - Read-only record of the conversion applied to the line.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Warehouse
entries.content:
The **Warehouse** in **DIGITZ ERP** represents a physical or logical location at which stock is held.

### Purpose

To maintain stock balances and valuation separately for each location, so that quantity and value are known per warehouse and not only in total.

### How It Works

Every stock ledger entry is recorded against a warehouse, and balances are therefore maintained per item **and** per warehouse. A warehouse can be associated with a **Company** and optionally with a **Project**, which allows stock held for a particular project to be tracked separately.

The Company's **Default Warehouse** setting supplies the warehouse used when a transaction does not specify one. A warehouse that is no longer in use can be marked **Disabled** rather than deleted, so historical ledger entries remain intact.

### Key Fields

- **Warehouse Name** - Name of the location.
- **Company** - Company the warehouse belongs to.
- **Project** - Optional project the warehouse is dedicated to.
- **Disabled** - Marks a warehouse as no longer available for new transactions.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Price List and Item Price
entries.content:
**Price Lists** and **Item Prices** in **DIGITZ ERP** hold the rates used when items are bought and sold.

### Purpose

To maintain rates centrally so that buying and selling documents pick up the correct price automatically, and to keep a history of how a rate has changed over time.

### How It Works

A **Price List** is marked as **Is Buying**, **Is Selling**, or both. The application ships with `Standard Buying` and `Standard Selling`, which are the defaults referenced by the Company configuration.

An **Item Price** links an item to a price list with a **Rate**, a **Unit**, and a **Currency**. Validity can be limited with **From Date** and **To Date**; a record without dates is open-ended and applies until superseded.

When the **Standard Selling Price** or **Standard Buying Price** is set on the **Item**, the corresponding Item Price record in the standard price list is created or updated automatically on save. The reverse can be suppressed on an individual Item Price record with **Do Not Update Price In Item**.

The Company settings **Update price list price with sales invoice** and **Update price list price with purchase invoice** determine whether transaction rates flow back into the price list.

### Validations

- Two Item Price records for the same item and price list cannot have overlapping date ranges.
- Only one open-ended Item Price record may exist for the same item and price list.

### Key Fields

- **Item** - The item being priced.
- **Price List** - The list the rate belongs to.
- **Rate** - The price of the item in the selected unit and currency.
- **Unit** - Unit the rate applies to.
- **Currency** - Currency of the rate.
- **From Date / To Date** - Optional validity period for the rate.
- **Is Selling / Is Buying** - Inherited from the price list to indicate where the rate applies.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Stock Ledger
entries.content:
The **Stock Ledger** in **DIGITZ ERP** is the single record of every stock movement and the basis of all stock valuation and reporting.

### Purpose

To hold one row per item movement per warehouse, carrying both the quantity effect and the value effect, so that the stock position and its valuation can be reconstructed for any date and time.

### How It Works

Each ledger row records **Qty In** or **Qty Out** together with the **Incoming Rate** or **Outgoing Rate**, and the resulting **Balance Qty**, **Balance Value**, and **Valuation Rate** for that item in that warehouse. Valuation follows the **moving average** method, so an inward movement at a new rate re-averages the valuation rate applied to subsequent issues.

Every row is stamped with its **Posting Date** (as a date and time), the **Voucher** type and **Voucher No** that produced it, and optionally the **Cost Center**, **Project**, and **Company**. The ledger is written by:

- **Purchase Receipt**, **Purchase Invoice**, and **Purchase Return**
- **Delivery Note**, **Sales Invoice**, and **Sales Return**
- **Stock Transfer**, **Stock Entry**, **Material Issue**, and **Stock Reconciliation**

Because the posting date carries a time component, documents are sequenced precisely. If a document is submitted with the same date and time as an existing voucher, the system advances the posting time by a few seconds so the ordering stays unambiguous; if it cannot find a free slot it stops the submission.

When a document is posted earlier than existing movements, the row is flagged as having later records and the reposting routine recalculates every affected row forward from that point.

### Key Fields

- **Item** and **Warehouse** - The stock position the row belongs to.
- **Posting Date** - Date and time of the movement, used to sequence the ledger.
- **Qty In / Qty Out** - Quantity received into or issued from the warehouse, in base units.
- **Incoming Rate / Outgoing Rate** - Rate at which the quantity moved.
- **Valuation Rate** - Moving average rate after the movement.
- **Balance Qty / Balance Value** - Resulting quantity and value held.
- **Change In Stock Value** - Value effect of the row.
- **Voucher / Voucher No** - Document that produced the movement.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Material Request
entries.content:
The **Material Request** in **DIGITZ ERP** records an internal request for materials, either to be purchased or to be transferred between warehouses, and routes it through an approval before it can be acted upon.

### Purpose

To capture what has been asked for, by whom, and by when — and to ensure that quantities are approved, and budgets respected, before any purchase or transfer takes place.

### How It Works

The request is raised with a **Purpose** of either `Purchase` or `Stock Transfer`, a **Required By** date, and a target warehouse. Each line names the item, the requested **Quantity**, and the unit, and can carry its own required-by date, source warehouse, and project.

Each line also has a **Quantity Approved**, which is what the approver actually sanctions. The document cannot be submitted until it is marked **Approved** and at least one line carries an approved quantity. On submission the system compares approved quantities with requested quantities and sets the **Status** to `Partially Approved` when any line was approved for less than it asked for.

Where budgets are in use, the request is checked against the budget allocated to the item or its item group, valued at the line's valuation rate. If the request would take cumulative usage past the allocated amount, submission is blocked.

As purchasing proceeds, **Qty Purchased** on each line records how much of the approved quantity has been procured, so an outstanding position is always visible.

### Key Fields

- **Purpose** - Whether the request results in a purchase or a stock transfer.
- **Required By** - Date the material is needed.
- **Source Warehouse / Target Warehouse** - Where the material moves from and to.
- **Items** - Requested items with quantity, unit, required-by date, and project.
- **Quantity Approved** - Quantity sanctioned by the approver for each line.
- **Approved** - Must be set before the document can be submitted.
- **Status** - `Requested`, `Approved`, `Partially Approved`, or `Rejected`.
- **Requested By** - User who raised the request.
- **Rejection Reason** - Recorded when a request is turned down.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Stock Transfer
entries.content:
The **Stock Transfer** in **DIGITZ ERP** moves stock from one warehouse to another within the same company.

### Purpose

To relocate goods between warehouses while preserving their value, so that quantities are correct at both locations and no gain or loss is created by the movement itself.

### How It Works

A transfer is entered with a **Source Warehouse** and a **Target Warehouse** at document level; individual lines may override either, allowing several warehouse pairs to be handled in one document. Any line left blank inherits the document-level warehouses.

On submission the system writes two stock ledger effects for each line — an issue from the source warehouse and a receipt into the target warehouse — using the item's **Qty In Base Unit** so that the movement is recorded in the stocking unit regardless of the unit entered.

Before posting, the available balance at the source warehouse is checked. If no stock exists, or the balance is less than the quantity being moved, the transfer is stopped — unless the Company has **Allow Negative Stock** enabled.

A stock transfer moves value between locations but does not change the total value of stock held, so it produces **no general ledger posting**. Where the transfer is dated earlier than existing movements, a **Stock Recalculate Voucher** is raised for both the source and the target so the affected ledger rows are recalculated forward.

### Validations

- The same combination of item, source warehouse, target warehouse, and unit cannot appear twice in one document.
- Sufficient quantity must exist at the source warehouse unless negative stock is allowed.
- A voucher cannot share its posting date and time with an existing transfer; the system advances the time automatically, and stops if no free slot is found.

### Key Fields

- **Source Warehouse / Target Warehouse** - Document-level default locations for the movement.
- **Items** - Items moved, with quantity, unit, rate, and per-line warehouses.
- **Qty In Base Unit** - Quantity actually posted to the ledger.
- **Date / Posting Time** - When the movement takes effect, editable with **Edit Posting Date And Time**.
- **Remarks** - Free text describing the reason for the transfer.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Material Issue
entries.content:
The **Material Issue** in **DIGITZ ERP** records the consumption of stock out of a warehouse into a project or a subcontracting job.

### Purpose

To take materials out of stock and charge their value to work in progress, so that project and job costs reflect the materials actually consumed.

### How It Works

An issue is raised with a **Purpose** of either `Project Consumption` or `Sub Contracting`, a **From Warehouse**, and a **Work In Progress Account**. Lines can be linked to a **Work Order**, **Project**, **BOQ**, **BOQ Execution**, or a **Sub Contracting Order Item**, so the consumption is attributable to the job it belongs to.

On submission the system issues each line from the warehouse at the item's current valuation and, for the total value issued, posts a general ledger entry that **credits the Inventory account** and **debits the Work In Progress account**. Stock value therefore moves out of inventory and into work in progress rather than being written off.

Availability is checked before posting: if no stock exists, or the balance is short of the quantity being issued, the document is stopped unless the Company allows negative stock.

### Validations

- The rate on an issued line cannot be zero.
- Sufficient quantity must exist in the issuing warehouse unless negative stock is allowed.
- A voucher cannot share its posting date and time with an existing issue.

### Key Fields

- **Purpose** - `Project Consumption` or `Sub Contracting`.
- **From Warehouse** - Warehouse the materials are issued from.
- **Work In Progress Account** - Account debited with the value of materials issued.
- **Project / Work Order / BOQ / BOQ Execution** - Job the consumption is charged to.
- **Sub Contracting Order** - Order the materials are issued against, when issuing for subcontracting.
- **Items** - Items issued with quantity, unit, rate, and the resulting net amount.
- **Net Total** - Total value issued, and the amount posted to work in progress.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Stock Entry
entries.content:
The **Stock Entry** in **DIGITZ ERP** brings materials back into a warehouse from a subcontracting job.

### Purpose

To receive materials returned by a subcontractor against the **Sub Contracting Order** and **Material Issue** they were issued under, so that unconsumed quantities re-enter stock and the job's material position stays accurate.

### How It Works

The document is raised with the **Purpose** `Sub Contracting Material Receipt` and is linked to the **Sub Contracting Order** and the **Material Issue** it reverses. Each line references the originating **Sub Contracting Order Item** or **Material Issue Item**, and shows **Qty In The Order** and **Qty Issued** alongside the quantity being received, so the receipt can be checked against what was issued.

On submission the received quantities are written into the stock ledger for the receiving warehouse, and the linked subcontracting order's status is updated to reflect the materials returned.

### Key Fields

- **Purpose** - `Sub Contracting Material Receipt`.
- **Sub Contracting Order** - The order the materials were issued against.
- **Material Issue** - The issue document being received back.
- **Warehouse** - Warehouse receiving the returned materials.
- **Items** - Items received, each linked to the order or issue line it came from.
- **Qty In The Order / Qty Issued** - Reference quantities shown for comparison against the receipt.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Stock Reconciliation
entries.content:
The **Stock Reconciliation** in **DIGITZ ERP** sets the quantity and valuation rate of items in a warehouse to a stated figure, and posts the resulting difference to the accounts.

### Purpose

To bring the system in line with a physical count, and to load opening stock when a company starts using the application.

### How It Works

The document is raised with a **Purpose** of either `Stock Reconciliation` or `Opening Stock`. Unlike a transfer or an issue, the quantity entered on each line is not a movement but the **resulting balance** — the system compares it with the balance already on record for that item and warehouse at the posting date and time, and derives the quantity in or out needed to reach it. The **Valuation Rate** entered on the line becomes the rate at which the resulting balance is held.

The value effect is posted to the general ledger. For the `Stock Reconciliation` purpose the difference is booked between the Company's **Inventory account** and its **Stock Adjustment account** — a rise in value debits inventory and credits stock adjustment, and a fall reverses the pair. For the `Opening Stock` purpose the opening value is posted against the opening balance accounts instead.

### Validations

- A reconciliation cannot be posted for an item that already has a stock entry dated **after** the reconciliation's posting date — the position must be set before later movements, not behind them.
- The same item and unit cannot be listed twice in one document.
- A voucher cannot share its posting date and time with an existing reconciliation.

### Key Fields

- **Purpose** - `Stock Reconciliation` for a physical count adjustment, or `Opening Stock` for initial balances.
- **Warehouse** - Warehouse being reconciled.
- **Items** - Items with the counted **Qty**, the **Valuation Rate** to hold them at, and the unit.
- **Stock Adjustment Account** - Account carrying the value difference.
- **Default Cost Center** - Cost center the adjustment is charged to.
- **Net Total** - Total value of the reconciled position.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Item to Item Transfer
entries.content:
The **Item to Item Transfer** in **DIGITZ ERP** moves every reference from one item code to another across the system.

### Purpose

To correct the situation where the same physical item has been created twice, by consolidating all history onto a single item code instead of leaving transactions split between duplicates.

### How It Works

The document names a **From Item** and a **To Item**. On submission the system rewrites the item reference — along with the item name and display name — in every table that carries it, so past and present documents all point at the surviving code.

The whole operation runs inside a database savepoint. If any part of the rewrite fails, everything is rolled back and no partial change is left behind. A summary of the tables touched and the number of rows updated is reported on completion and stored on the document.

### Restrictions

- Only the **Administrator** may execute an Item to Item Transfer.
- Both items must exist, and the From Item and To Item cannot be the same.

### Key Fields

- **From Item** - The item code being retired.
- **To Item** - The item code that will carry the consolidated history.
- **From Item Name / To Item Name** - Names shown for confirmation before submission.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Stock Reposting and Recalculation
entries.content:
**Stock Reposting** in **DIGITZ ERP** keeps valuation correct when documents are entered out of chronological order.

### Purpose

Under moving average valuation, every movement depends on the ones before it. When a document is posted with a back date, all later movements for that item were calculated without it. Reposting recalculates those later rows so balances, valuation rates, and cost of goods sold end up as though the entry had always been there.

### How It Works

When a stock document is submitted or cancelled with a posting date earlier than existing movements, the system raises a **Stock Recalculate Voucher** recording which voucher triggered it, its date and time, and a status of `Not Started`. Stock Transfers raise one for the source warehouse and one for the target.

The **Stock Repost** settings record how far reposting has progressed — the **Last Processed Stock Ledger**, its **Last Processed Posting Date**, and a **Posting Status** which is set to `In Process` while a run is under way so that two runs cannot overlap.

A scheduled job runs **hourly** and works through the outstanding ledger rows: duplicate ledger entries are cleaned, each affected row is recalculated forward in time, and a **Stock Repost Detail** record is written for the rows processed. Once the ledger is rebuilt, the item's **Stock Balance**, **Stock Value**, and **Valuation Rate** are refreshed on the Item master, and the **cost of goods sold** on the affected Delivery Notes, Sales Invoices, and Sales Returns is updated to the corrected valuation.

Reposting can also be triggered manually for all items or for a single item when a specific correction is needed.

### Key Fields

- **Stock Recalculate Voucher** - Raised per triggering document, carrying the voucher, its date and time, and processing status.
- **Last Processed Stock Ledger** - The point reposting has reached.
- **Posting Status** - Guards against overlapping reposting runs.
- **Stock Repost Detail** - Log of the ledger rows processed in a run.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Stock Reports
entries.content:
The **Stock Reports** in **DIGITZ ERP** present the stock ledger from several angles — as a movement trail, as a closing position, and as a period summary.

### 1. Stock Ledger Report

The full movement trail. For each item it lists every voucher in date order with the **Voucher Type**, **Voucher No**, **Warehouse**, **Opening Qty**, **Qty In** and **Incoming Rate**, **Qty Out** and **Outgoing Rate**, the resulting **Valuation Rate**, and the running balance. This is the report to use when a balance or a valuation needs to be traced back to the documents that produced it.

### 2. Stock Ledger Summary Report

The same movements condensed — voucher, date, warehouse, opening quantity, quantity in and out, and closing balance — without the rate detail, for a quicker read of what moved.

### 3. Stock Balance Register

The closing position rather than the movements: **Stock Qty**, **Unit**, **Valuation Rate**, and **Stock Value** per item and warehouse, with the **Total Stock Value** across the selection. This is the report that reconciles to the inventory account.

### 4. Stock Movement Report

Movement of stock over a period, drawn from the stock ledger, for reviewing activity rather than balances.

### 5. Daily Stock Report

A day's activity broken down by the reason it occurred — **Opening Qty**, **Stock Recon Qty**, **Purchase Qty**, **Purchase Return Qty**, **Sales Qty**, **Sales Return Qty**, **Transfer In Qty**, **Transfer Out Qty**, and the closing **Balance Qty**. It shows not just how much stock changed but which process changed it.

### 6. Daily Stock Report Summary

The same information condensed to **Opening Qty**, **Stock Recon**, **Qty In**, **Qty Out**, and **Balance Qty**, available in a consolidated form or broken down date by date.

### 7. Project Stock Ledger Report

The movement trail restricted to a project, showing the same voucher-level detail with the **Project** alongside — used where materials are held and consumed against specific projects.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Buying Module Overview
entries.content:
The **Buying Module** in **DIGITZ ERP** covers procurement from the moment a requirement is raised to the moment the supplier bill is recorded and, where necessary, goods are sent back.

The cycle runs **Material Request → Purchase Order → Purchase Receipt → Purchase Invoice**, with **Purchase Return** handling goods returned to the supplier. Each stage carries its quantities and values forward into the next, and each records how much of the preceding document has been consumed — so the outstanding position is visible at every step.

The stages divide cleanly by what they affect:

- **Purchase Order** is a commitment. It creates neither stock nor accounting entries; it records what was ordered and tracks how much has since been purchased against it.
- **Purchase Receipt** handles the **physical movement**. It brings goods into the warehouse and recognises their value as received but not yet billed.
- **Purchase Invoice** handles the **financial posting** — supplier liability, expense, and tax. It is documented under the Accounting module; see [Purchase Invoice](#purchase-invoice).
- **Purchase Return** reverses both, sending goods back and reducing the amount payable.

Buying also participates in wider controls. **Budgets** are checked when a Purchase Order or Purchase Receipt is saved, so an item or item group cannot be committed past its allocation. Where a **Project** is set, the purchase cost is accumulated on the project. Where an item is a **Fixed Asset**, receiving it creates the asset record automatically.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Supplier
entries.content:
The **Supplier** in **DIGITZ ERP** is the party master for everything the company buys.

### Purpose

To hold one record per supplier — identity, contact details, tax registration, credit arrangement, and default pricing terms — which every buying document draws from.

### How It Works

Suppliers are identified by **Supplier Name**, which is also the record's name. Each supplier carries a **Default Price List**, from which buying documents pick up their rates, and may carry a **Default Terms** record; where **Use Default Supplier Terms From Company Settings** is set, the company-level terms are applied instead.

The credit arrangement is held on the supplier as **Credit Days** and a **Credit Amount Limit**, and flows into the credit fields on purchase documents.

For tax, the supplier's **TRN No** is recorded and carried onto purchase documents as the tax identifier. **Tax Not Applicable** marks a supplier whose transactions are outside the tax regime.

Suppliers are classified by **Supplier Group** — a simple master of a name and a disabled flag — which is used for grouping and analysis. A supplier no longer traded with can be marked **Disabled** rather than deleted, so historical documents remain intact.

### Key Fields

- **Supplier Name** - Name and identifier of the supplier.
- **Supplier Group** - Classification the supplier belongs to.
- **Default Price List** - Price list buying documents take rates from.
- **Credit Days / Credit Amount Limit** - The credit arrangement agreed with the supplier.
- **TRN No** - Tax registration number, carried onto purchase documents.
- **Tax Not Applicable** - Marks the supplier as outside the tax regime.
- **Address, City, State, Emirate, Country** - Location details, also assembled into a **Full Address**.
- **Contact Person, Designation, Contact Mobile No, Phone No, Mobile No, Email** - Contact details.
- **Default Terms / Use Default Supplier Terms** - Terms and conditions applied to the supplier's documents.
- **Bank Details** - Free-text bank information used when paying the supplier.
- **Disabled** - Retires the supplier without removing history.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Purchase Order
entries.content:
The **Purchase Order** in **DIGITZ ERP** records a commitment to buy goods or services from a supplier.

### Purpose

To state what has been ordered, at what price, and on what terms — and to track how much of that order has since been received or invoiced, so the pending position is always known.

### How It Works

An order is raised against a **Supplier** for a **Warehouse**, with rates drawn from the selected **Price List**. Each line records the item, quantity, unit, rate, applicable **Tax**, and any line discount; the totals section carries the gross total, line-item discounts, tax total, additional discount, round off, and rounded total, with the rounded total also written out **in words**.

The order records how it is to be settled. **Credit Purchase** with **Credit Days** and **Payment Terms** marks it as payable later; otherwise a **Payment Mode** must be chosen and the full rounded total is treated as paid.

A Purchase Order is a commitment only — it produces **no stock ledger entry and no accounting entry**. Its effect is tracked through **Qty Purchased** on each line, which is maintained as purchase receipts and invoices are raised against the order. From those quantities the order's **Status** is derived:

- **Pending** - nothing has been purchased against the order yet.
- **Partial** - at least one line has been purchased for less than it ordered.
- **Completed** - every line has been fully purchased.

Where a line has been purchased for **more** than was ordered, the order is still marked as completed but an excess-allocation warning is raised.

An order may be raised from an approved **Material Request**, in which case each line keeps a reference back to the request line and updates that line's purchased quantity as the order is saved, cancelled, or deleted. Where a **Project** is set, the project's purchase cost is updated from the gross totals of its submitted orders. The **For Sub Contracting** flag marks an order raised for subcontracted work.

### Validations

- A **Payment Mode** must be selected when the order is not a credit purchase.
- The same item cannot appear in more than one row with the same display name.
- Each item is checked against the **budget** allocated to it or to its item group; if the order would take cumulative usage past the allocation, submission is blocked.
- A voucher cannot share its posting date and time with an existing Purchase Order; the system advances the posting time automatically and stops if no free slot is found.

### Key Fields

- **Supplier** - Party the order is placed with, along with the supplier address and TRN.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are expected into.
- **Price List** and **Rate Includes Tax** - How rates are sourced and whether they are tax-inclusive.
- **Credit Purchase / Credit Days / Payment Terms / Payment Mode** - The settlement arrangement.
- **Items** - Ordered items with quantity, unit, rate, tax, discount, and cost center.
- **Qty Purchased** - Quantity of each line already purchased against the order.
- **Material Request** - The approved request the order was raised from.
- **Project / Default Cost Center** - Costing dimensions carried onto downstream documents.
- **For Sub Contracting** - Marks the order as raised for subcontracted work.
- **Status** - `Pending`, `Partial`, or `Completed`, derived from purchased quantities.
- **Terms / Terms and Conditions** - Contractual text printed with the order.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Purchase Receipt
entries.content:
The **Purchase Receipt** in **DIGITZ ERP** records the physical receipt of goods from a supplier into a warehouse.

### Purpose

To bring goods into stock at the point they are received, and to recognise their value as received but not yet billed — so that the stock position is correct even before the supplier's invoice arrives.

### How It Works

A receipt is raised against a **Supplier** and a **Warehouse**, and may be generated from a **Purchase Order**, in which case the supplier, terms, totals, and pending item lines are carried across.

On submission the receipt does two things:

**Stock.** Each line is received into the warehouse at its rate, written to the stock ledger in the item's base unit. Where the receipt is dated earlier than existing movements for an item, a **Stock Recalculate Voucher** is raised so the later ledger rows are recalculated forward.

**Accounts.** For the value of goods excluding tax, the receipt **credits the Stock Received But Not Billed account** and **debits the Inventory account**. Tax and the supplier liability are not posted here — they belong to the Purchase Invoice, which reverses the received-but-not-billed balance when the bill is recorded.

Where a received item is a **Fixed Asset**, an **Asset** record is created automatically from the line — carrying the item, asset category, gross value, and posting date, and placed at the company's default asset location. If the company has no default asset location configured, a `Default Asset Location` is created and linked to the company.

The receipt tracks its own billing state through **Status**: it is created as **To Bill**, and moves to **Billed** when a Purchase Invoice is raised against it — returning to **To Bill** if that invoice is cancelled. A separate **Posting Status** of `Pending`, `Started`, or `Posted` records how far the receipt's own stock and ledger postings have progressed.

As quantities are received, **Qty Purchased** on the originating Purchase Order lines is updated and the order's status is re-derived.

### Validations

- Each item is checked against the **budget** allocated to it or to its item group.
- A voucher cannot share its posting date and time with an existing receipt.

### Key Fields

- **Supplier** and **Supplier Inv No / Supplier Inv Date** - The party and their reference for the delivery.
- **Purchase Order** - The order the receipt is raised against.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are received into.
- **Items** - Received items with quantity, unit, rate, tax, and discount.
- **Status** - `To Bill` until a Purchase Invoice is raised, then `Billed`.
- **Posting Status** - Progress of the receipt's stock and ledger postings.
- **Payment Schedule** - Planned settlement dates and amounts for the receipt.
- **Project / Default Cost Center** - Costing dimensions for the receipt.
- **Update Rates In Price List** - Writes the received rates back to the price list.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Purchase Return
entries.content:
The **Purchase Return** in **DIGITZ ERP** records goods sent back to a supplier and reduces the amount payable accordingly.

### Purpose

To take returned goods out of stock and reverse their financial effect — reducing the supplier liability, the inventory value, and the input tax originally claimed.

### How It Works

A return is raised against a **Supplier** from a **Warehouse**, and its lines reference the original **Purchase Invoice** line being returned. The **Invoices** table records which invoices the return is set against.

On submission the return issues the goods out of the warehouse and posts the reversal to the general ledger:

- The **Accounts Payable account is debited** with the rounded total, reducing what is owed to the supplier.
- The **Inventory account is credited** with the value excluding tax.
- The **Tax account is credited** with the tax total, reversing the input tax.
- Any **round off** is posted to the round off account.

Where the return is not a credit purchase, payment postings are made as well, so a return against a cash purchase settles immediately rather than sitting on the payable.

If the return carries a **Payment Schedule**, the corresponding schedule entries are rebuilt against the return, replacing any that existed before.

### Validations

- The quantity returned cannot exceed what remains available on the original purchase line. The check is cumulative — all other returns already raised against that line are counted, so a line cannot be over-returned across several documents.
- Stock must exist in the warehouse and be sufficient for the quantity being returned, unless the Company has **Allow Negative Stock** enabled.

### Key Fields

- **Supplier** - Party the goods are returned to.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are issued from.
- **Items** - Returned items with quantity, unit, rate, tax, and the reference to the original purchase line.
- **Invoices** - The purchase invoices the return is set against.
- **Credit Purchase** - Determines whether the return reduces the payable or settles immediately.
- **Payment Schedule** - Rebuilt against the return where settlement is scheduled.
- **Posting Status** - Progress of the return's stock and ledger postings.
- **Project / Default Cost Center** - Costing dimensions for the return.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Buying Document Flow
entries.content:
The buying documents in **DIGITZ ERP** are connected by rules that decide which document may be raised from which, and what is still outstanding.

### Material Request to Purchase Order

An approved **Material Request** with the purpose `Purchase` can be turned into a **Purchase Order**. Only lines with an approved quantity that has not yet been fully ordered are carried over, and each order line keeps a reference back to the request line so the request's purchased quantity stays current.

### Purchase Order onward — two routes, not both

From a submitted Purchase Order the goods can be recorded either through a **Purchase Receipt** first, or straight onto a **Purchase Invoice**. The system enforces that only one route is taken for a given order:

- A **Purchase Receipt** cannot be created when a submitted Purchase Invoice already references the order without a receipt.
- A **Purchase Invoice** cannot be created when the order is already linked to a Purchase Receipt — the invoice must be raised from that receipt instead.
- The Purchase Order must be **submitted** before an invoice can be created from it.
- Creation stops if the order has **no pending items** left, and if any line has a conversion factor of zero or less.

Use the receipt route when goods arrive before the bill; use the direct invoice route when the bill accompanies the goods.

### Purchase Receipt to Purchase Invoice

A **Purchase Invoice** can be generated from a Purchase Receipt, carrying the supplier, warehouse, terms, dates, and lines across. On submission the receipt's status becomes **Billed**, and the value held in Stock Received But Not Billed is cleared into the supplier liability. Cancelling the invoice returns the receipt to **To Bill**.

### Purchase Return

A **Purchase Return** is raised against **Purchase Invoice** lines rather than against orders or receipts, since it is the billed quantity that determines what may be returned.

### What each stage affects

| Document | Stock | General Ledger |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase Order | — | — |
| Purchase Receipt | Goods in | Inventory debited, Stock Received But Not Billed credited |
| Purchase Invoice | Goods in, when raised without a receipt | Supplier liability, expense, and tax |
| Purchase Return | Goods out | Payable debited; inventory and tax reversed |

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Buying Reports
entries.content:
The **Buying Reports** in **DIGITZ ERP** present the purchase documents as registers, as itemwise detail, and as period analysis.

### Registers

**Purchase Register**, **Purchase Order Register**, and **Purchase Return Register** list the documents of each type over a period with their supplier, dates, and values — the document-level view of what was ordered, purchased, and returned.

### Itemwise detail and summaries

Each register has an itemwise pair. The **Itemwise Register** reports break the documents down to their individual lines, and the **Itemwise Summary Report** consolidates those lines by item:

- **Purchase Itemwise Register** and **Purchase Itemwise Summary Report**
- **Purchase Order Itemwise Register** and **Purchase Order Itemwise Summary Report**
- **Purchase Return Itemwise Register** and **Purchase Return Itemwise Summary Report**

Use the register when a specific transaction must be traced, and the summary when the question is how much of an item was bought or returned in total.

### Analysis

**Periodic Purchase Analysis Report** and **Periodic Expense Analysis Report** present purchases and expenses across periods for comparison rather than for tracing individual documents.

**Purchase Payment Analysis Report** shows purchases against what has been paid, for reviewing the settlement position with suppliers.

**Projectwise Purchase Receipt Report** groups received goods by project, for projects where materials are purchased and consumed against a specific job.

**Buying Chart - Top Supplier Purchases** ranks suppliers by purchase value, giving a quick view of where spend is concentrated.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Selling Module Overview
entries.content:
The **Selling Module** in **DIGITZ ERP** covers the sale of goods and services from the first quotation through to delivery, invoicing, and any goods returned.

The cycle runs **Quotation → Sales Order → Delivery Note → Sales Invoice**, with **Sales Return** handling goods taken back from the customer. Each stage carries its quantities and rates forward, and each records how much of the preceding document has been consumed — so what remains outstanding on an order is always visible.

The stages divide by what they affect:

- **Quotation** is an offer. It creates neither stock nor accounting entries, and must be marked **Won** before it can be converted.
- **Sales Order** is a confirmed commitment. It also posts nothing; it tracks how much of what was ordered has since been delivered or invoiced.
- **Delivery Note** handles the **physical movement** — goods leave the warehouse and their cost is recognised.
- **Sales Invoice** handles the **financial posting** — customer receivable, income, and tax. It is documented under the Accounting module; see [Sales Invoice](#sales-invoice).
- **Sales Return** reverses both, bringing goods back into stock and reducing the receivable.

**Tab Sales** provides a shorter path for counter sales, producing a Sales Invoice directly.

Progress across the whole cycle can be followed on the **Sales Flow** dashboard, which brings every stage of a customer transaction onto one screen; see [Sales Flow](#sales-flow).

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Customer
entries.content:
The **Customer** in **DIGITZ ERP** is the party master for everything the company sells.

### Purpose

To hold one record per customer — identity, contacts, delivery locations, tax registration, credit arrangement, and default pricing — which every selling document draws from.

### How It Works

Customers are identified by **Customer Name**. Each carries a **Default Price List**, from which selling documents take their rates, and may carry **Default Terms**; where **Use Default Customer Terms** is set, the company-level terms apply instead.

The credit arrangement is held as **Credit Days** and a **Credit Amount** limit, and flows into the credit fields on selling documents. The customer's **Tax Id** is carried onto sales documents as the tax registration.

Customers are classified by **Customer Group** — a name and a disabled flag — and located by **Area**, which is itself grouped by **Emirate**. A **Salesman** can be assigned, linking the customer to an Employee for reporting. Multiple **Delivery Locations** can be recorded and selected as the ship-to location on individual documents.

Where a customer originated as a lead, the **Prospect** field links back to the **Sales Prospect** record it was converted from.

Two flags affect reporting and access: **Exclude From Showing In SOA** keeps the customer out of statement of account output, and **Disabled** retires a customer without removing history.

### Customer-specific pricing

Beyond the default price list, the **Item** master carries a **Customer Prices** table. When a Sales Order is submitted, the rate used for each line is written back as that customer's rate for that item, dated with the order's posting date — and an existing entry is only replaced when the new date is later. Whether these remembered rates are then applied to new documents is controlled by **Use Customer Last Price** in the Company settings.

### Key Fields

- **Customer Name** - Name and identifier of the customer.
- **Customer Group** - Classification the customer belongs to.
- **Default Price List** - Price list selling documents take rates from.
- **Credit Days / Credit Amount** - The credit arrangement agreed with the customer.
- **Tax Id** - Tax registration number, carried onto sales documents.
- **Delivery Locations** - Ship-to locations selectable on selling documents.
- **Salesman** - Employee responsible for the account.
- **Area, Emirate, Country, Address Line 1 and 2** - Location details, also assembled into a **Full Address**.
- **Contact Person, Designation, Phone, Mobile No, Email** - Contact details.
- **Default Currency** - Currency the customer is billed in.
- **Prospect** - The Sales Prospect this customer was converted from.
- **Exclude From Showing In SOA** - Omits the customer from statement of account output.
- **Disabled** - Retires the customer without removing history.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Quotation
entries.content:
The **Quotation** in **DIGITZ ERP** records a priced offer made to a customer or a prospect.

### Purpose

To state what is being offered, at what price, and on what terms — and to record the outcome of the offer so that won and lost business can be analysed.

### How It Works

A quotation is raised for a **Customer** or, through **Lead From = Prospect**, for a **Sales Prospect** that has not yet become a customer. Rates come from the selected **Price List**, and each line carries the item, quantity, unit, rate, tax, and any discount. The rounded total is also written out **in words**.

A quotation posts **nothing** — no stock movement and no ledger entry. It is an offer until its outcome is recorded.

The outcome is held in **Status**, which is `Pending`, `Won`, or `Lost`. A won quotation can record a **Won Reason** and a lost one a **Lost Reason**, both drawn from their own master lists so the reasons stay consistent and reportable.

**A quotation must be marked Won before a Sales Order can be created from it.** Attempting to convert a quotation in any other status is refused. The conversion option is only offered while the quotation has not already been used — once a Sales Order, Delivery Note, or Sales Invoice exists against it, it cannot be converted again. Where the quotation was raised for a prospect, the system first checks that a Customer exists for that prospect.

A quotation can be **duplicated** into a fresh quotation carrying the same customer, terms, totals, and lines — the practical way to issue a revision, alongside the **Rev.No** and **Rev Date** fields kept for print. Recurring sets of lines can be pulled in from a **Quotation Items Template** rather than entered by hand.

Where the company has **Manual Quotation No** enabled, the quotation is named by the number entered on the document rather than by the automatic series.

### Key Fields

- **Customer** or **Prospect** with **Lead From** - Who the offer is made to.
- **Status** - `Pending`, `Won`, or `Lost`; must be `Won` to convert.
- **Won Reason / Lost Reason** - The recorded outcome, from their master lists.
- **Price List** and **Rate Includes Tax** - How rates are sourced and whether they are tax-inclusive.
- **Items** - Offered items with quantity, unit, rate, tax, and discount.
- **Quotation Item Template** - A saved set of lines to populate the quotation from.
- **Salesman** - Employee the offer is credited to.
- **Ship To Location** - Delivery location selected from the customer's locations.
- **Qtn Validity, Rev.No, Rev Date, Subject, Attn** - Details carried onto the printed quotation.
- **Terms / Terms and Conditions** - Contractual text printed with the offer.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Sales Order
entries.content:
The **Sales Order** in **DIGITZ ERP** records a confirmed commitment to supply a customer.

### Purpose

To state what the customer has ordered, at what price and on what terms, and to track how much of that order has since been delivered or invoiced.

### How It Works

An order is raised for a **Customer** against a **Warehouse**, and records the customer's own purchase order through the mandatory **LPO No** and **LPO Date**. It may be created from a won **Quotation**, in which case the quotation is linked.

A Sales Order posts **nothing** — no stock movement and no ledger entry. Its effect is tracked through **Qty Sold** on each line, which is maintained as delivery notes and sales invoices are raised against the order. From those quantities the order's **Status** is derived:

- **Pending** - nothing has been delivered or invoiced against the order yet.
- **Partial** - at least one line has been supplied for less than it ordered.
- **Completed** - every line has been fully supplied.

Where a line has been supplied for **more** than was ordered, an excess-allocation warning is raised.

On submission the order also **remembers its pricing**: for each line, the rate is written back to the customer's entry in the item's Customer Prices table, dated with the order's posting date.

From a Sales Order the system can generate a **Delivery Note** or a **Sales Invoice**, each built only from the quantity still outstanding — the pending quantity is calculated as ordered quantity less quantity already sold. If nothing is pending, generation is refused. An order can also be **duplicated** into a new order carrying the same customer, terms, totals, and lines.

### Key Fields

- **Customer** - Party the order is for, with address, tax id, and balance shown.
- **LPO No / LPO Date** - The customer's own purchase order reference; both required.
- **Quotation** - The won quotation the order was created from.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are to be supplied from.
- **Items** - Ordered items with quantity, unit, rate, tax, and discount.
- **Qty Sold** - Quantity of each line already delivered or invoiced.
- **Status** - `Pending`, `Partial`, or `Completed`, derived from sold quantities.
- **Credit Sale / Credit Days / Payment Terms / Payment Mode** - The settlement arrangement.
- **Salesman** and **Ship To Location** - Attribution and delivery location.
- **Default Cost Center** - Costing dimension carried onto downstream documents.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Delivery Note
entries.content:
The **Delivery Note** in **DIGITZ ERP** records goods leaving the warehouse for a customer.

### Purpose

To take goods out of stock at the point they are dispatched and recognise their cost, so that the stock position and cost of sales are correct whether or not the invoice has been raised.

### How It Works

A delivery note is raised for a **Customer** from a **Warehouse**, and is usually generated from a **Sales Order** — carrying the customer, terms, totals, and the outstanding lines across. Because a note can draw on more than one order, the **Sales Orders** table is rebuilt from the line references each time the document is saved, listing every order the delivery draws on.

On submission the delivery note does two things:

**Stock.** Each line is issued from the warehouse and written to the stock ledger in the item's base unit, valued at the item's current moving average rate.

**Accounts.** For the resulting cost of goods sold, the note **credits the Inventory account** and **debits the Cost of Goods Sold account**. Revenue, receivable, and tax are not posted here — they belong to the Sales Invoice.

As quantities are delivered, **Qty Sold** on the originating Sales Order lines is updated and each affected order's status is re-derived. The same happens in reverse when the note is cancelled or deleted.

The **Is Delivered** flag records that the goods have physically reached the customer, separately from the document having been submitted.

### Validations

- Stock must exist in the warehouse and be sufficient for the quantity being issued, unless the Company has **Allow Negative Stock** enabled.
- An item with no prior stock ledger entry must have a valuation rate on the Item master; otherwise the system stops with *"Please provide a valuation rate for the item, as there is no existing purchase invoice for it."*
- A voucher cannot share its posting date and time with an existing delivery note; the system advances the posting time automatically and stops if no free slot is found.

### Key Fields

- **Customer** - Party the goods are delivered to, with address and balance.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are issued from.
- **Sales Orders** - The orders this delivery draws on, rebuilt from the line references.
- **Items** - Delivered items with quantity, unit, rate, and the reference to the order line.
- **Is Delivered** - Marks that the goods have reached the customer.
- **LPO No / LPO Date** - The customer's purchase order reference, carried from the order.
- **Posting Status** - Progress of the note's stock and ledger postings.
- **Ship To Location** and **Salesman** - Delivery location and attribution.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Sales Return
entries.content:
The **Sales Return** in **DIGITZ ERP** records goods taken back from a customer and reverses their financial effect.

### Purpose

To bring returned goods back into stock and unwind the original sale — reducing the receivable, the income recognised, the output tax, and the cost of goods sold.

### How It Works

A return is raised for a **Customer** into a **Warehouse**, and its lines reference the original **Sales Invoice** line being returned. The **Invoices** table records which invoices the return is set against.

On submission the return receives the goods back into the warehouse and posts the reversal to the general ledger:

- The **Accounts Receivable account is credited** with the rounded total, reducing what the customer owes.
- The **Income account is debited** with the value excluding tax.
- The **Tax account is debited** with the tax total, reversing the output tax.
- The **Inventory account is debited** and the **Cost of Goods Sold account credited** with the cost of the returned goods, so cost of sales is unwound at the same value it was recognised at.
- Any **round off** is posted to the round off account.

Where the return is not a credit sale, payment postings are made as well, so a return against a cash sale is settled immediately rather than sitting on the receivable.

The return also keeps the surrounding documents consistent: quantities on the originating **Sales Invoice** and **Delivery Note** lines are adjusted, any **Receipt Schedule** entries are rebuilt against the return, and the status of each affected **Sales Order** is re-derived.

### Validations

- The quantity returned cannot exceed what remains available on the original sales line. The check is cumulative — all other returns already raised against that line are counted, so a line cannot be over-returned across several documents.

### Key Fields

- **Customer** - Party the goods are returned from.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are received back into.
- **Items** - Returned items with quantity, unit, rate, and the reference to the original sales line.
- **Invoices** - The sales invoices the return is set against.
- **Credit Sale** - Determines whether the return reduces the receivable or settles immediately.
- **Posting Status** - Progress of the return's stock and ledger postings.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Tab Sales
entries.content:
**Tab Sales** in **DIGITZ ERP** is a shorter entry screen for over-the-counter sales, where the full order-to-delivery cycle is unnecessary.

### Purpose

To record a sale in a single step, without raising a quotation, order, and delivery note first — while still producing the same accounting and stock effect as a normal sale.

### How It Works

Tab Sales has its own entry page and is filled in like a sales document: customer, warehouse, payment mode, and lines with quantity, unit, rate, and tax.

Behind it, the document maintains a **linked Sales Invoice**. As the Tab Sales record is built and saved, the corresponding Sales Invoice is created or brought back into step with it. When the Tab Sales document is submitted, that linked Sales Invoice is submitted with it — and the invoice, not the Tab Sales record, is what posts to stock and to the ledger.

This means the accounting behaviour of a counter sale is exactly that of a Sales Invoice, described under [Sales Invoice](#sales-invoice). Tab Sales is the faster way to reach it.

**Auto Save Delivery Note** additionally produces the delivery documentation for the sale where the goods are handed over at the same time.

### Validations

- Stock availability is checked for the items being sold, as it is on any document that issues stock.
- An item with no prior stock ledger entry must carry a valuation rate on the Item master.
- A voucher cannot share its posting date and time with an existing record.

### Key Fields

- **Customer** - Party the sale is made to.
- **Warehouse** - Location the goods are sold from.
- **Items** - Sold items with quantity, unit, rate, tax, and discount.
- **Credit Sale / Payment Mode / Payment Account** - How the sale is settled.
- **Auto Save Delivery Note** - Produces the delivery documentation alongside the sale.

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Selling Document Flow
entries.content:
The selling documents in **DIGITZ ERP** are connected by rules that decide which document may be raised from which, and what is still outstanding.

### Quotation to Sales Order

A **Quotation** must be marked **Won** before it can be converted; the system refuses to proceed otherwise. Conversion is only offered while the quotation is unused — once a Sales Order, Delivery Note, or Sales Invoice exists against it, it cannot be converted again. Where the quotation was raised against a **Prospect**, the system first checks that a Customer exists for that prospect.

### Sales Order onward

From a submitted Sales Order the goods can be recorded either through a **Delivery Note** first, or straight onto a **Sales Invoice**. In both cases only the **pending quantity** is carried over — ordered quantity less quantity already sold — and generation is refused when nothing is pending:

> *"No pending items in the Sales Order to generate a Delivery Note."*

The system tracks whether an order has already been taken down either route, so that a single order is not accidentally delivered and invoiced twice over for the same quantity.

Because the pending quantity drives everything, an order can be supplied across several deliveries or invoices, each drawing what remains. A single **Delivery Note** can likewise draw on more than one Sales Order, and the orders it draws on are listed on the note.

### Delivery Note to Sales Invoice

A **Sales Invoice** raised against delivered goods references the delivery notes it bills, so the same goods are not invoiced twice.

### Sales Return

A **Sales Return** is raised against **Sales Invoice** lines rather than against orders or deliveries, since it is the invoiced quantity that determines what may be returned. Returning goods adjusts the originating invoice and delivery note quantities and re-derives the status of every affected Sales Order.

### What each stage affects

| Document | Stock | General Ledger |
|---|---|---|
| Quotation | — | — |
| Sales Order | — | — |
| Delivery Note | Goods out | Inventory credited, Cost of Goods Sold debited |
| Sales Invoice | Goods out, when raised without a delivery note | Receivable, income, and tax |
| Sales Return | Goods in | Receivable credited; income, tax, and cost of sales reversed |

entries.title: DIGITZ ERP — Selling Reports
entries.content:
The **Selling Reports** in **DIGITZ ERP** present the sales documents as registers, as itemwise detail, and as analysis.

### Registers

**Quotation Register**, **Sales Order Register**, **Delivery Note Register**, **Sales Register**, and **Sales Return Register** list the documents of each type over a period with their customer, dates, and values — the document-level view of what was quoted, ordered, delivered, invoiced, and returned.

### Itemwise detail and summaries

Each register has an itemwise pair. The **Itemwise Register** reports break the documents down to their individual lines, and the **Itemwise Summary Report** consolidates those lines by item:

- **Quotation Itemwise Register** and **Quotation Itemwise Summary Report**
- **Sales Order Itemwise Register** and **Sales Order Itemwise Summary Report**
- **Delivery Note Itemwise Register** and **Delivery Note Itemwise Summary Report**
- **Sales Itemwise Register** and **Sales Itemwise Summary Report**
- **Sales Return Itemwise Register** and **Sales Return Itemwise Summary Report**

Use the register when a specific transaction must be traced, and the summary when the question is how much of an item was sold or returned in total.

### Daily activity

**Daily Report** and **Daily Report Detailed** present a day's selling activity, the detailed variant going down to the individual transactions behind the totals.

### Analysis

**Periodic Sales Analysis Report** presents sales across periods for comparison rather than for tracing individual documents.

**Sales Receipt Analysis Report** shows sales against what has been received, for reviewing the collection position.

**Customer Outstanding Summary Report** presents the balance owed per customer.

**Projectwise Billing Report** groups billing by project, for work sold and invoiced against a specific job.

**Top Customer Sales Report** and **Sales Chart - Top Customer Sales** rank customers by sales value, as a table and as a chart, giving a quick view of where revenue is concentrated.

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Overview
entries.content:
**Every Relationship — Nurtured with Intelligent CRM.**

DIGITZ CRM is a complete customer relationship and sales management system. It captures leads, qualifies them, converts them into deals, tracks every conversation along the way, and rolls won business up into revenue you can report on — all inside one governed system.

What makes DIGITZ CRM different is that it keeps **relationship building** and **deal making** as two distinct disciplines. Acquiring and qualifying a lead is not the same job as progressing a deal to a close, so each has its own pipeline, its own stages and its own working screen. Nothing is forced into a single mixed funnel.

### What You Can Do

- Maintain partner and customer relationships as **Associations**, with a full engagement history
- Capture and qualify **Leads**, with stage-by-stage tracking of how each relationship matures
- Convert qualified leads into **Opportunities**, with commercial guardrails that prevent premature conversion
- Run the day from a personal **Action Centre** — activities, planned work, task inbox and calendar
- See any lead or deal in a single pane with **360 views**, including a complete relationship timeline
- Track meetings, tasks, checklists and compliance documents against every record
- Roll won revenue automatically up to the Lead, the Association and the Strategy
- Measure your team with **KRA/KPI performance** records and over 30 built-in reports

### Who It Is For

- **Sales executives** — a personal daily working surface and a clear view of their own pipeline
- **Sales managers** — branch and team pipelines, conversion rates, activity levels and performance scoring
- **Business owners** — cross-funnel KPIs, revenue visibility by strategy, and audit-ready history

*Use the listing on the left to browse each area of the application.*

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Key Concepts
entries.content:
Understanding six ideas is enough to use DIGITZ CRM confidently.

### The Relationship Hierarchy

```
Strategy          how you go to market (e.g. Sales Process, Sales Partnership)
  └── Association   the relationship or partner account
        └── Lead      an acquisition and qualification record
              └── Opportunity   a deal you are trying to win
```

Every Lead belongs to an Association, and every Opportunity comes from a Lead. This chain is what allows won revenue to be reported at any level — a single deal, a whole relationship, or an entire go-to-market strategy.

### The Six Concepts

#### 1. Strategy

The highest level — how you approach the market. Two are provided out of the box: **Sales Process** (direct selling) and **Sales Partnership** (selling through partners). Revenue is summarised against each.

#### 2. Association

The relationship account: the company or partner you are dealing with. It carries contacts, engagement history, an association stage, an action plan and its own revenue summary. A **Default Association** is created for you, so you are never blocked when creating your first lead.

#### 3. Lead

An acquisition and qualification record — the company or person you are working to qualify. A Lead holds identity, contacts, ownership (branch, executive, distributor), and all the working detail: activities, meetings, tasks, checklist, documents and remarks.

#### 4. Opportunity

A deal. It must originate from a Lead and must list at least one product or service. It carries the commercial detail — probability of winning, expected closing date, competitors, quotation and order values, and the quote-to-invoice trail.

#### 5. Executive

Your salespeople are recorded as **Executives**, linked to a user account, a branch and optionally a distributor. The Executive record is what drives data access: it decides which leads, deals and activities a person sees, and which fields they may change.

#### 6. Stage

Both Leads and Opportunities move through stages. Stages are configurable — you can rename them, reorder them, or add your own — because the system never relies on the *name* of a stage. Instead every stage is classified by **type**, which is what the software actually acts on.

| Record | Stage types available |
| --- | --- |
| Lead | Open · Qualified · Nurturing · Disqualified · Inactive |
| Opportunity | Open · Won · Lost · On Hold |

### Benefits

- Your stage names can match how your business actually speaks, without breaking any reporting
- Revenue is meaningful at every level of the hierarchy, not just per deal
- Access control follows your real organisation — branches, distributors and executives

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Setting Up
entries.content:
### Overview

DIGITZ CRM installs with a working set of master data, so you can start entering leads immediately. This section covers what is created for you and what you should configure before rolling out to a team.

### What Is Created Automatically

On installation the system creates:

| Master | Seeded values |
| --- | --- |
| Lead Stages | New · Contact Attempted · Contacted · Engaged · Qualified · Nurturing · Disqualified · Inactive |
| Opportunity Stages | New Opportunity · Discovery · Requirement Confirmed · Solution Proposed · Quotation Sent · Negotiation · Approval Pending · Verbal Commitment · Won · Lost · On Hold |
| Association Stages | New Association · Contacted · Exploring Synergies · Onboarding · Active Partnership · Inactive |
| Strategies | Sales Process · Sales Partnership |
| Association | Default Association |
| Activity Types | Call · Email · Online Meeting · Physical Meeting · WhatsApp · Task |
| Sales Effort Target Types | Sales Conversion / Proposals / Activities per month |
| Project Execution Milestones | Milestone 1 – 8 |
| KRA Group | Default KRA Group |

### Recommended Setup Order

#### 1. Branches

Create a Branch for each office or location. Branches carry address, currency and contact details, and are the primary way data is partitioned between teams.

#### 2. Distributors and Business Partners

If you sell through distributors, create them and assign each to a branch. The first distributor created for a branch automatically becomes that branch's default.

#### 3. Executives

Create one Executive per salesperson and link it to their user account, their branch, and — where relevant — their distributor. This single step configures their data access: the system automatically restricts that user to their branch and grants access to their distributor.

#### 4. Product Portfolio

List the products and services you sell. Every Opportunity must reference at least one, and product-wise revenue reporting depends on this list.

#### 5. Review Your Stages

Rename or reorder the seeded stages to match your sales process. Two settings matter most:

- **Sequence** — controls the order that stages appear in the pipeline boards
- **Allows Opportunity Creation** — marks the lead stages from which a deal may be created (by default, only *Qualified*)

#### 6. Checklist Templates

Create a CheckList Task Template of the steps that should be completed on every lead or every opportunity, and mark it as the default. New records will pick it up automatically.

#### 7. CRM Settings

Finally, review the CRM Settings screen to switch on the field rules your business needs — see [CRM Settings](#settings).

### Benefits

- A usable system from day one, with no blank-screen setup
- Access control configured as a by-product of recording your team, not as a separate exercise
- Stage names and sales steps that match how your business already works

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Associations
entries.content:
### Overview

An **Association** is the relationship account — the company, partner or institution you deal with. It sits above leads, so every lead you create is anchored to a relationship rather than floating on its own.

### Purpose

Associations let you:

- Keep one authoritative record of a company you deal with repeatedly
- See the total engagement history of a relationship, not just individual leads
- Track partner relationships through their own lifecycle stages
- Report revenue by relationship as well as by deal
- Record referral chains — which association introduced which

### How It Works

Each Association holds:

| Area | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Identity | Name, company, rank, market segment, industry, website |
| Contact | Primary contact plus a full contacts table |
| Address | Address lines, emirate, country |
| Relationship | Association stage, strategy, referred-by association |
| Ownership | Branch, sales executive, currency |
| Engagement | Activities and planned schedules |
| Planning | An action plan table with feedback and rating per action |
| Revenue | Fiscal-year revenue rolled up from won deals |
| Counters | Opportunity count and closed deal count |

Associations move through their own stages — from **New Association**, through **Contacted** and **Exploring Synergies**, to **Onboarding** and **Active Partnership**, or to **Inactive**.

### Key Features

#### 1. Relationship-First Structure

Because every lead must belong to an association, you always know which relationship a piece of business came from.

#### 2. Create a Lead Directly

A lead can be created straight from an association — identity, contacts and address are all copied across, so nothing is retyped.

#### 3. Referral Tracking

The *referred association* field records who introduced whom, letting you see which partners actually generate business.

#### 4. Revenue Summary

Won deals roll up automatically into the association's fiscal-year revenue table.

### Benefits

- One place to understand everything happening with a company
- Partner performance becomes measurable, not anecdotal
- Repeat business is visible rather than scattered across unrelated leads

entries.title: DIGITZ CRM — Leads
entries.content:
### Overview

A **Lead** is the acquisition and qualification record — the organisation you are working to turn into a customer. It is the busiest record in DIGITZ CRM and holds everything your team does before a deal exists.

### Purpose

The Lead record exists to answer three questions at any moment:

1. Who is this, and who owns them?
2. How far have we got in qualifying them?
3. What has actually been done, and what is planned next?

### How It Works

A Lead is created from scratch, from an Association, or from a Prospect record. It is named after the lead name, and requires an association, a branch and a country.

Information is organised into these areas:

| Area | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| Identity | Lead name, company name, rank, lead stage, remarks |
| Primary contact | Contact person, designation, phone, mobile, email, WhatsApp |
| Contacts | A table of every other person at the organisation |
| Address | Address lines, emirate, country, website |
| Segmentation | Market segment, industry, campaign |
| Ownership | Branch, sales executive, distributor, partner type, currency |
| Qualification | Lead stage, first client visit date |
| Working tabs | Activities, schedules, meetings, meeting tasks, checklist, tasks, documents, remarks |
| Revenue | Fiscal-year revenue rolled up from won deals |

### Key Features

#### 1. Ownership Is Enforced, Not Suggested
